title: Downstream Guardian: tiered eviction & fallback playbook
creator: Diego Morales
description: Problem: During regional blips and backend slowdowns we see cascading token latency spikes and increased tail errors from Redis/Kafka/DB dependencies. Current behavior: large bursts cause connection exhaustion, timeouts, and whole-request failures. Objective: implement a deterministic, tenant-aware downstream 'guardian' that applies tiered eviction, adaptive admission, circuit breaking and staged fallbacks so customer-facing SLOs (p50/p95 latency, availability) are preserved while minimizing silent correctness regressions. This ticket defines SLOs, control-plane policies, runtime hooks, and an operational playbook for gradual rollout.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Define tenant-level SLOs and dependency SLO budget allocations (percentages) and document in console SLO page.
2) Implement a runtime admissions layer that enforces per-region connection caps and soft-priority lanes (system, prod-high, prod-low, dev) with eviction order.
3) Add circuit-breaker policy that transitions dependencies through CLOSED -> PROBING -> OPEN -> DEGRADED with metrics and cooldowns configurable per-dependency.
4) Provide 3 staged fallback handlers: cached-KV read, replica-only reads, and synthetic partial responses (with explicit response metadata) and ensure telemetry flags correctness regressions.
5) Rollout in canary (region-b) and validate with chaos/latency-injection: no more than 2x p95 increase for 90% of tenants, and availability degradation limited to tenants flagged as 'best-effort'.
6) Publish runbook and add alert run links in Console; include automated remediation snippets for pagers.
design_notes: We avoid increasing request latency by doing admission gating at request admission time (before queuing large batches). Use token-bucket shaped admission for burst smoothing and a sliding-window SLO budget to allow short bursts. Eviction order: non-critical replicas -> dev lanes -> cached reads -> read-only replica -> synthetic partial -> hard-fail. Circuit breaker thresholds tuned to latency percentiles and error-rate rather than absolute RTT to reduce sensitivity to transient network jitter. Use Redis TTL-based soft fallback; for Kafka, prefer consumer-lag-aware backoff and graceful windowed sampling. Trade-offs: synthetic partial responses reduce utility but preserve availability; aggressive shedding risks data correctness and must be tenant-gated.
implementation_plan: A) SLO model: define per-tenant SLO objects and dependency budgets (storage in config service).
B) Admission service: implement admission proxy as a sidecar hook in the runtime with per-tenant queues and dynamic cap enforcement.
C) Circuit breaker: library-level hooks for dependencies (redis/kafka/db) with centralized state sync and metrics export.
D) Fallbacks: implement cached-KV layer and a replica-readpass; add explicit response metadata headers (X-Redwood-Fallback: cached-kv|replica|synthetic).
E) Observability: new dashboards (per-tenant fallback rate, eviction counts, probe success rates) and SLO burn reports.
F) Tests: unit + integration + chaos experiments. Prepare canary runbook and rollout automation.
test_plan: Unit tests: breaker state transitions, admission throttle logic, fallback selection priority.
Integration: local cluster using test redis/kafka instances verifying fallback handlers and metadata propagation.
Chaos: inject increased latency and partial timeouts to redis/kafka in canary region; measure p50/p95 and fallback rates.
Load tests: synthetic multi-tenant load with heavy tail distribution to ensure eviction respects tenant priorities.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature flag off in production. Stage 2: enable for internal tenants and infra trials (two small tenants). Stage 3: canary in region-b with 5% of traffic for 48h. Stage 4: progressive ramp to 25% then 100% same-region. Stage 5: enable multi-region routing policies for failover. Rollback via FF kill and automatic circuit open for runtime if error budget breached.
monitoring_and_alerting: New alerts: high fallback-rate (>5% baseline) per-tenant, >10% eviction rate, circuit open sustained >5m, probe-fail rate >3/min. Dashboards: per-dep latency heatmaps, tenant SLO burn, admission queue depth. Add pager runbooks linking to the runbook below. Create synthetic queries that assert correctness of fallback metadata.
